title: Standardize supplemental labels, autofill resilience, and validation layering for composed address inputs
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background:
We maintain a wide set of composed input patterns for multi-part data (address, phone, credit card). The address pattern in particular has accumulated multiple local variations across products: differing label treatments, inconsistent autofill anchors, and duplicated inline helper text. These inconsistencies cause flicker during browser autofill, poor screen reader announcements, and developer confusion when mapping native autofill attributes to our tokenized components.

Problem statement:
1) Supplemental labels (short descriptors above groups, e.g., "Delivery address (optional)") are rendered inconsistently between compact/dense layouts and cause layout jumps when validation messages appear.
2) Browser autofill often populates only some subfields (postal code, city) which causes partial state and inconsistent validation triggers.
3) Validation layering and error prioritization across sub-fields is not defined: multiple simultaneous errors produce competing inline messages and errant focus cycling.

Goals:
- Define a deterministic protocol for supplemental/section labels and where they should live relative to input groups in compact vs. default density.
- Make autofill behavior resilient: avoid layout shift and preserve hint/placeholder clarity when partial autofill occurs.
- Define validation layering rules for composed inputs so a single canonical message and focus target are chosen in multi-error states.
- Provide token guidance for spacing, label sizes, and color usage that integrates with our current density tokens and contrast rules.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Supplemental label pattern:
   - Treat supplemental label as a sibling block above the group with role=\"group\" and aria-labelledby referencing a generated ID.
   - For compact density, reduce the label to a single-line condensed token (token.label.supplemental-compact) that does not collapse the group margin when an inline message appears.
2) Autofill resilience: 
   - Add a small, zero-height prefix container for autofill anchors to capture browser events and apply an "autofill-stabilize" class that preserves computed height during input value changes.
   - On change events from autofill, run a 50ms debounce to batch visual updates (minimize flicker).
   - Map recommended HTML autocomplete attributes for composed address fields and include them in the component API by default (autocomplete: \"street-address\", separate autocomplete values for locality/region/postal-code).
3) Validation layering: 
   - Create a prioritization matrix: global group-level error > field-level critical error (required/malformed) > soft suggestions. Only the top-priority message is shown inline; additional errors are surfaced via aria-describedby on the visible message and available in the Console error breakdown.
   - Focus routing: on submit, focus the first sub-field with a field-level critical error. If none, focus the group container and expose the group-level message.
4) Tokens and theming: 
   - Introduce three new tokens: token.label.supplemental-size, token.label.supplemental-gap, token.autofill.stabilize-duration. Document usage across densities.

Accessibility considerations:
- Use role=\"group\" + aria-labelledby for supplemental labels so screen readers announce the section name before individual inputs.
- Ensure the single visible error is referenced by aria-describedby for all relevant inputs while providing a programmatic list of hidden errors for assistive tech via aria-errormessage when necessary.
- Test NVDA, VoiceOver, and a11y tree for common browsers where autofill behavior differs (Chrome, Safari).

Implementation notes for engineering:
- Expected component changes: AddressFieldGroup (new props: supplementalLabel, stableAutofill: true, validationPolicy: \"layered\").
- CSS: introduce autofill-stabilize utility. Ensure no layout regressions across densities.
- Tests: unit + visual snapshots for compact/default densities, integration test with synthetic autofill events to assert no height shift and stable label visibility.
- Docs: Figma spec pages and Component docs with code samples (React) showing autocomplete mapping.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design tokens and component API documented in the Design System site.
- Figma components updated and synced with code tokens.
- Engineering PR merges with passing visual regression tests and unit coverage.
- Accessibility checklist passed: screen reader flow documented; no new a11y regressions.
- Rollout plan documented and staged behind feature flag for 2-week canary.

Rollout and migration plan:
- Phase 1: Opt-in flag for new AddressFieldGroup behavior; update two internal apps to opt-in and run monitoring.
- Phase 2: Default opt-in after 2 weeks if no regressions; provide migration guide for teams with custom CSS.
- Phase 3: Deprecate legacy classnames in next minor release after migration window.
